content:
This month, Apple will unveil its first foldable iPhone, reportedly to be called the iPhone Ultra. The device will feature a 5.5-inch outer screen and a 7.6-inch inner screen. Back in July, Samsung launched its new Galaxy Z Fold 8, which uses the same two screen sizes.

Whether you believe Samsung launched this phone just to beat the iPhone Ultra to market is another matter—but regardless, seeing the Galaxy Z Fold 8 gives us an early look at what the iPhone Ultra will actually be like in real-world use.

Reviewers who got the Galaxy Z Fold 8 early have been posting tons of comparison photos with other devices on Twitter. Since the iPhone Ultra and Galaxy Z Fold 8 are similar in size, these photos give us a preview of what the iPhone Ultra will look and feel like in the real world.

Ray Wong posted several photos comparing the Galaxy Z Fold 8 with the previous-generation iPad mini, highlighting how the phone essentially lets you pocket an iPad mini-sized screen—with even slimmer bezels.

Meanwhile, enthusiast Shishir shared comparison shots of the iPhone 13 mini alongside the Galaxy Z Fold 8. The iPhone 13 mini is slightly taller than the foldable, but similarly compact. For those who miss the iPhone mini lineup, the iPhone Ultra might offer a fairly close experience.

Personally, after seeing the Galaxy Z Fold 8 in person last week, I'm more excited about the iPhone Ultra than ever. The two devices should look nearly identical in form factor (though the iPhone Ultra will have rounded corners)—so this might be the best preview we'll get of what Apple has really been working on before the official reveal in September.

Of course, you can also check out images of dummy models for further comparison.
